Bug_Details:
Futures.getChecked requires a checked exception type with a standard constructor. The passed exception type must not be a RuntimeException, and it must expose a
public constructor whose only parameters are of type String or Throwable.
getChecked will reject any other type with an IllegalArgumentException.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is that the code is trying to call a non-existent method getChecked() on a Future object. This is due to a typo or misunderstanding of the Java Future API.
Trigger_Explanation: The call to buggyFuture.showBug() in the test triggers the bug in the line future.get() of the showBug method, as future.get() is incorrectly called instead of a non-existing method getChecked().
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results are 'OK (1 test)' which means that the test passed without any errors or exceptions. However, the bug in the code is a compilation error because there is no getChecked method in Future, which was not executed during the test. Therefore, the test results do not confirm the presence of the described bug.
